extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A new dataset with the goal of advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition by placing the question of object recognition in the context of the broader question of scene understanding. This is achieved by gathering images of complex everyday scenes containing common objects in their natural context. Objects are labeled using per-instance segmentations to aid in precise object localization. The dataset contains photos of 91 objects types that would be easily recognizable by a 4 year old. With a total of 2.5 million labeled instances in 328k images.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár. Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. arXiv:1405.0312v3 [cs.CV], 21 Feb 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr using queries for pairs of object categories or object and scene categories. Additionally, a filtering step removed iconic images. At most 5 photos per photographer within a short time window were downloaded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Flickr photos with searchable metadata and keywords.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered to remove near-duplicates using a detection method and grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize near-duplicate images across splits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation pipeline with three stages: (1) Category labeling: workers used a hierarchical approach with 11 super-categories, dragging icons onto images. 8 workers per image. (2) Instance spotting: workers placed crosses on each instance of a category, with priming from previous stage. 8 workers per image. (3) Instance segmentation: workers segmented each instance using a modified interface from Bell et al. [16]. Training tasks required for each category. Verification step with 3-5 workers judged segmentation quality. For images with >10 instances of a category, remaining instances marked as 'crowds' with a single segment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Worker precision and recall analysis for category labeling: union of 8 AMT workers achieved greater recall than any expert. For unambiguous examples, probability all 8 annotators missing a case is at most 0.004. Over 99% of object categories not later rejected as false positives are detected given 8 annotators. For instance spotting, similar analysis with 8 annotators. For segmentation, training task filtered out bad workers (approximately 1 in 3 passed). Verification stage: segmentations with less than 4 of 5 favorable votes were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into two parts: first half released in 2014, second half in 2015. The 2014 release contains 82,783 training, 40,504 validation, and 40,775 testing images. The cumulative 2015 release contains 165,482 train, 81,208 val, and 81,434 test images. The dataset will evolve and grow over time; up to date information is available online at http://mscoco.org/.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images of people (person category) and may contain faces, but no explicit personal information is collected.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on common objects recognizable by a 4 year old, and images were collected from Flickr, which may introduce biases in terms of cultural representation and scene types. The selection of categories was based on votes from co-authors, considering frequency, usefulness, and diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only includes 'thing' categories, not 'stuff' categories. Some categories were omitted in the 2014 release due to too many instances, ambiguity, or too few instances. The dataset may not generalize to all object recognition tasks, especially those requiring fine-grained categorization or rare objects.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and validation for object detection and segmentation algorithms. The dataset is designed for detecting non-iconic views, contextual reasoning, and precise 2D localization of objects.
